# Concurrency & Lifecycle Requirements Checklist: Limited Drop Reservation Service

**Purpose**: Reviewer gate for the quality of requirements on concurrency, inventory integrity, hold
lifecycle and expiration, before implementation. These items test the written requirements, not the code.
**Created**: 2026-10-06
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [data-model.md](../data-model.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope**: Focus is concurrency & integrity, and lifecycle & expiration. API/error contract and
resilience/ops are deferred to a later checklist run (append to a new file such as `api.md`).

## Requirement Completeness: Inventory Integrity

- [ ] CHK001 Is the no-oversell invariant stated as a precise, checkable formula relating total, available, ACTIVE and CONFIRMED units? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements defined for what "allocated" means for an ACTIVE hold that is past expiry but not yet processed (does it still count against availability)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK003 Is all-or-nothing allocation specified for multi-unit requests competing for the last few units, with no partial grants? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the spec require each hold-state change and its matching inventory change to happen together or not at all, for every mutating operation (place, cancel, expire)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-026]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for how the system must behave if returning units would exceed the drop's total (an "impossible" invariant breach)? [Gap, Plan research §3]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the fixed total quantity stated as immutable for the life of the drop, including during active holds? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]

## Requirement Clarity: Concurrency

- [ ] CHK007 Is "simultaneous" or "concurrent" defined precisely enough to test (requests overlapping in time, from any number of clients and service instances)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "exactly one wins" defined for each competing pair: confirm vs expire, cancel vs expire, cancel vs confirm? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the outcome the losing request receives specified for each race pair (rejection reason vs. idempotent success)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025, §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "any number of service instances" bounded or qualified so that the requirement can be verified? [Measurability, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK011 Does the spec state that correctness must not depend on in-process coordination of a single instance? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023, Constitution IX]

## Requirement Completeness: Repeated & Duplicate Requests

- [ ] CHK012 Are idempotency semantics specified for hold placement when identical requests (same request key) arrive concurrently, not just sequentially? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009, §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the comparison rule for "same request details" fully defined (which fields must match: drop, quantity, customer)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the replay response defined when the original hold has since changed state (confirmed, cancelled or expired)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK015 Is request-key retention defined beyond "as long as the hold exists", given holds are never deleted in v1 (is retention effectively permanent)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-009, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK016 Is it specified that the same request key used by two different customers is treated as independent? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK017 Are repeated confirm and repeated cancel requirements consistent with the general "reject invalid transitions" rule, with the exception stated explicitly? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, §FR-021]

## Requirement Clarity: Lifecycle & State Transitions

- [ ] CHK018 Is the complete transition table specified, including every (current state × requested action) combination and its outcome? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011–FR-017, Data Model]
- [ ] CHK019 Are final states (CONFIRMED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED) explicitly declared immutable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the rejection reason for acting on an EXPIRED hold distinguished from a generic invalid transition, and is this consistent across confirm and cancel? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, §FR-017, §FR-029]
- [ ] CHK021 Does the spec define whether a rejected confirm or cancel on an overdue-but-unprocessed hold also settles it to EXPIRED, or only reports it? [Ambiguity, Spec Story 2 §AS-2, §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the wrong-customer behavior specified consistently for retrieve, confirm and cancel, and does it never change state? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022a]

## Requirement Clarity: Expiration & Time

- [ ] CHK023 Is the expiry boundary unambiguous: is a confirm at exactly `expiresAt` rejected, with "passed" in FR-015 matching "at or after" in Edge Cases? [Conflict, Spec §FR-015, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the release-time boundary unambiguous: is a hold at exactly `startsAt` allowed? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK025 Is the 10-second release bound defined as measured from `expiresAt` to units being available for new holds, not just to the status change? [Measurability, Spec §FR-018, §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK026 Are requirements defined for expiry when the primary data store was unavailable at the time a hold became due (catch-up bound after recovery)? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases, §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK027 Is the "service clock is the single authority" assumption consistent with multiple instances, and is acceptable clock skew stated? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions, Plan research §13]
- [ ] CHK028 Is it specified whether changing the configured hold duration affects existing ACTIVE holds? [Gap, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK029 Is expiry-processing idempotency (run twice, run concurrently on several instances) stated as a requirement rather than only a plan decision? [Completeness, Spec Story 3 §AS-3, Edge Cases]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK030 Are SC-001 and SC-002 repetition counts and pass conditions defined so that a single failing run fails the criterion? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK031 Can "units returned exactly once" be verified purely from observable state (the invariant in CHK001), without inspecting internals? [Measurability, Spec §FR-020, §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK032 Do acceptance scenarios exist for every race pair in CHK008 and for repeated expiry processing? [Coverage, Spec Stories 2–4]
- [ ] CHK033 Is the SC-005 condition ("caching and messaging unavailable") specific about which failure modes count (down, slow, returning stale data)? [Clarity, Spec §SC-005, §FR-027]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK034 Is the assumption that overdue holds briefly block availability (≤10s) explicitly accepted as a fairness trade-off in the spec? [Assumption, Spec Clarifications, §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK035 Are requirements traceable: does every concurrency and lifecycle FR map to at least one acceptance scenario or success criterion? [Traceability]

## Notes

- Items are unchecked until a reviewer approves the requirement quality. `/speckit-implement` reads
  checklist state but does not modify markers.
- Items with `[Gap]`, `[Conflict]` or `[Ambiguity]` (CHK005, CHK015, CHK021, CHK023, CHK026, CHK028) are
  the likeliest to need spec edits.
